bullets: Index funds are not a strategy — they're the absence of one; the second-order effect of that framing is the part most people miss.
Vanguard's structure pioneered low costs, and ignoring that structural foundation means rebuilding it from scratch a year later.
Framing the market reaction first, then looking at fundamentals, reverses the order most decisions follow — internalizing this sequence makes the rest of the decisions easier.
Tools like Bloomberg and Morningstar make the framing-first trade-off visible when built into the decision flow rather than bolted on later.
Risk management for individual investors is mostly behavioral rather than technical — a pattern observed holding across three different teams.
Small-value tilts are a position that was revised over time, with the change of mind observed in practice at teams using Wealthfront and Vanguard.
Frame cross-cuts every other trade-off in index investing, which makes it the connective thread rather than a standalone topic.
